semantics.evidence: Original problem: examine each bit, capture changes from 1 in one clock cycle to 0 the next; output remains 1 until active high synchronous reset; all sequential logic positive edge.
semantics.sampling: At each rising edge remember the current in vector for comparison on the next rising edge.
semantics.capture: When reset is low, each out bit becomes its old value OR (previous sampled input bit is 1 AND current input bit is 0).
semantics.reset: At a rising edge with reset high, clear all out bits with priority over capture. Sample in on that edge as well.
semantics.initialization: No initial value is specified; no initial block or artificial power-up initialization is added.

numeric.operation: Independent bitwise logic with no signed arithmetic or cross-bit effects

verification.oracle: Per-bit behavioral model based on successive positive-edge input samples and sticky capture until synchronous reset.
cases: reset between clock edges has no immediate effect
verification.sampling: Drive inputs away from positive edges; check after nonblocking updates and before next edge.
verification.termination: Fatal on mismatch, bounded timeout, PASS only after all checks

specification_ambiguities.issue: Reset behavior for input history register is not explicitly specified.
specification_ambiguities.resolution: History samples in on every rising edge, including reset; reset clears only captured output. This follows the stated reset of captured output and comparison of consecutive clock cycles.

specification_ambiguities.issue: Power-up values and behavior before the first input sample/reset are unspecified.
specification_ambiguities.resolution: Leave registers uninitialized; verification asserts defined output only after a synchronous reset and defined history after sampling.
